channel.title: LC Insight
channel.description: Read the chain, not the rumors. Crypto market news and on-chain analysis.

item.title: Rumor vs record: 4 of 6 crash claims hold up, led by bitcoin ETFs' $3.46 billion November outflow
item.description: A list of crash-week numbers spread widely over the weekend. We checked six lines against CoinMarketCap and CoinGecko: four are true, while the IBIT record and the 60-day Coinbase premium could not be checked.

item.title: ETF & Whale Flows, November 24: $1.37 billion left bitcoin ETFs in five straight days
item.description: U.S. spot bitcoin funds lost money for a fifth straight trading day on Monday, November 23, though the daily outflows keep shrinking. Ether funds took in money for the first time since November 13.

item.title: Pearl hit a record $2.48 on Monday, then slipped 8% by early evening
item.description: The AI mining coin climbed about 21% from midnight ET to a new high at 4:55 p.m. ET, just above its October record, while bitcoin went nowhere. By 7:10 p.m. ET it was back at $2.29.

item.title: Rumor vs record: bitcoin buys 17 ounces of gold, still 39% above its March low
item.description: Bitcoin has lost 15% against gold since November 1, and gold has held up better all year. But bitcoin was cheaper in gold in March, and gold itself is 36% below its record. We checked five claims.

item.title: 6 senators ask Treasury to give state stablecoin issuers the same shield as federal applicants
item.description: Treasury's draft rule gives federal applicants with a waiver up to 12 months of cover once the stablecoin law takes effect. Three Republicans and three Democrats say state-licensed issuers deserve the same.

item.title: Singapore MAS DPT license: PSA rules, capital, fees and process
item.description: Crypto firms serving customers in Singapore need a Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) license for digital payment token (DPT) services under the Payment Services Act. They apply as a standard or major payment institution, with base capital of S$100,000 or S$250,000.

item.title: The week's top shark made $1.27 million, then bought $396,000 of EVAA as it fell 43%
item.description: Only 23 of 99 sharks DeepSea tracks made money this week, and 71 lost. The best of them, Hold8771, spent about $592,000 in seven minutes on Sunday morning, on EVAA and on bitcoin.

item.title: Rumor vs record: XRP Ledger users fell 15%, not 60%. Four more weekend claims checked
item.description: A headline that the XRP Ledger lost 60% of its users spread overnight. XRPSCAN's counts show the drop only if you compare a record day with a day that is not over. We checked it and four other viral weekend claims.

item.title: WASTED memecoin rose 247% in two days, but its trading volume is down 98% from the peak
item.description: The Ethereum token tops CoinGecko's trending list on Sunday. Its record came on Friday. Daily trading volume, near $49.7 million on its first day in CoinGecko's data, has shrunk to $880,000.

item.title: XRP Ledger payments doubled to 1.19 million a day in November, even as XRP fell 30%
item.description: XRPSCAN's ledger counts show twice as many payments per day as in mid-October, and nearly four times the fees burned. But the busiest week is behind it, and U.S. XRP funds have not had an inflow day since October 29.

item.title: Crypto exchange license by country: UAE, Singapore, EU, UK, Hong Kong, US
item.description: Every major market has its own crypto exchange license: VARA in Dubai, MAS in Singapore, MiCA in the EU, FCA registration in the UK, the SFC regime in Hong Kong and FinCEN plus state licenses in the US. Each regulator publishes a register you can check.

item.title: Pieverse sets a record $3.92 as its market value tops $1 billion
item.description: PIEVERSE jumped about 10% in its last hour to a new high early Sunday, beating the $3.64 record from November 18. It is up about 103% in a week.

item.title: Venice (VVV) jumped 25% in a day to about $25, four times bitcoin's 6% gain
item.description: The private-AI token climbed from about $20.10 to $25.06 between 1 a.m. ET Saturday and 1 a.m. ET Sunday, November 22. Coinbase carried the most trading, and VVV is still about 27% below its September record.

item.title: Treehouse's 23.1 million TREE airdrop closes Wednesday; unclaimed tokens go to its treasury
item.description: Season 2 of Treehouse's airdrop set aside 23.1 million TREE, 2.31% of supply, and the claim window ends at 2:00 a.m. ET on November 25. The pot is worth about $667,000 at Sunday's price, with TREE 98% below its record.

item.title: Sharks sent $10.2 million of stablecoin tokens out in a day, $4 million in one Tron trade
item.description: DeepSea's 24-hour table shows shark wallets sending out about twice the stablecoins they took in during the bounce. One Arbitrum wallet shed $1.97 million of Aave USDC debt tokens.

item.title: Bitcoin bounced 5%, but the five biggest dollar stablecoins grew just $122 million
item.description: USDT supply barely moved after Friday's $442 million drop, and its price slipped further to $0.9984. USDC won back $415 million of its crash-week dip.

item.title: Bitcoin touched $60,799 as Hyperliquid bets grew $50 million and funding turned negative
item.description: Open bets on Hyperliquid's bitcoin contract rose to $1.11 billion through Saturday's rebound, still well below Friday's $1.23 billion. Trading volume halved and more markets paid shorts.

item.title: Rumor vs record: bitcoin's $55,150 low broke July's bottom in the midterm fourth quarter
item.description: As bitcoin bounced 5%, a cycle claim spread: midterm years make fresh lows late in the fourth quarter. CoinMarketCap and CoinGecko records show it held in 2018 and 2022, only loosely in 2014, and 2026 has already followed it.

item.title: Sharks bought $830,649 of WBTC on Arbitrum in the bounce and sold $900,306 of staked ether
item.description: Bitcoin rose 5% in a day, and DeepSea's shark wallets flipped to net buyers of bitcoin on Arbitrum after selling $894,130 the day before. They sold staked ether, ARB and OP.

item.title: Rain (RAIN) fell 11% in an hour late Saturday, even as bitcoin rose 5% on the day
item.description: RAIN slid from about $0.00355 to $0.00316 between 10 and 11 p.m. ET on November 21, a new 24-hour low. Only about $11.6 million traded against a market value of $2.3 billion.

item.title: Derive jumped 27% in the crash as volume quadrupled to $20.8 million, led by Upbit
item.description: Three large tokens rose while almost everything else fell: Derive (DRV), Bitway (BTW) and Venice (VVV). Exchange data show where the buying happened. We found no primary source that explains the moves.

item.title: Rumor vs record: bitcoin is down 25% in November, its worst month since June 2022
item.description: After the overnight crash, a line spread that bitcoin slid as much as 23% in November and that the 2022 bear market is back. We checked each part against CoinMarketCap and CoinGecko price history. The fall is bigger than claimed, but 2022 was far worse.

item.title: Solana ETFs drew $4.7 million in crash week while ether funds lost $1.24 billion in four weeks
item.description: Of the U.S. spot bitcoin, ether, solana and XRP fund groups, only solana's had a weekly inflow, thanks to one Monday. Ether funds have had just two inflow days since late October, and XRP funds lost $11.1 million on the week.

item.title: Bitcoin fell 14% in a week, but mining difficulty is set to jump 10% and fees sit at 51 cents
item.description: A week after a 9.13% cut, blocks are arriving fast enough that mempool.space projects a 10% rise in about 864 blocks. Fees stayed tiny through the sell-off: about 51 cents a transaction.

item.title: Ether fell 14% in eight days, yet its staking exit line shrank 42% to 152,865 ETH
item.description: The crash did not send stakers rushing for the door. Validator Queue shows 820,241 ETH still waiting to be staked, more than five times the ether waiting to leave.

item.title: Bitcoin bounced 4%, yet top Hyperliquid traders' shorts grew to $606 million
item.description: The 88 big Hyperliquid wallets DeepSea tracks are still 93% short on bitcoin. One $42 million short from $56,948, close to the night's low, is now losing money.

item.title: Bitcoin bounced 4% in 45 minutes to $57,952, an hour after its lowest price since 2024
item.description: Bitcoin climbed from $55,637 to $57,952 early Saturday and ether jumped 5.4% to $1,640, CoinGecko data show. Both are still down more than 6% in a day.

item.title: Bored Ape floors held in ETH but lost 31% in dollars since November 2 as ether slid
item.description: Eight NFT blue chips barely moved in ETH as the market crashed, but in the last day all fell in dollars except Moonbirds. CryptoPunks are worth $265 million less than on November 2, by CoinGecko's count.

item.title: USDT shrank $442 million in one step and slipped to $0.9982 as bitcoin crashed
item.description: CoinGecko's data show USDT's supply flat for a day, then down $442 million Friday evening. USDC fell $649 million and won back $418 million. Tether's Ethereum treasury is down to $862 million.

item.title: Binance's wallets lost 4,857 bitcoin in the crash but took in $1.12 billion of USDT
item.description: In about 18 hours, bitcoin fell nearly 10% and the coins in Binance's listed wallets shifted: less bitcoin, more dollar tokens. Bitget lost 1,140 bitcoin, while OKX added 1,042.

item.title: HYPE fell 13% to $57, and its Hyperliquid futures bets shrank $76 million since Friday
item.description: Hyperliquid's own token fell harder than bitcoin and ether. Open bets on its main futures market dropped to $527 million, while top traders added to their shorts and now sit on paper gains as a group.

item.title: Ether fell under $1,600, and top Hyperliquid traders more than doubled their longs to $76M
item.description: The 55 wallets DeepSea tracks on ether went from 91% short to 79% short in a day. Most of the new bets on a rise were opened near $1,600, and the biggest one uses just 3x leverage.

item.title: Bitcoin fell to $56K, and Smart trader #72's $93 million short is gone from the board
item.description: The wallet behind Friday's biggest bitcoin short now holds only $10.2 million in USDC and shows an $8.4 million weekly gain on DeepSea. Top Hyperliquid traders cut their bitcoin shorts by $203 million.

item.title: Rumor vs record: bitcoin at $55,780 is below every October 2024 close, back to September
item.description: As bitcoin slid below $56,000 early Saturday, posts and headlines said it hit its lowest since October 2024, that crypto lost $200 billion and that billions in bets were wiped out. We checked six claims against price, market and exchange data.

item.title: Bitcoin ETFs lost $1.30 billion this week, including $126.8 million on Friday
item.description: U.S. spot bitcoin funds had a fourth straight outflow day as bitcoin broke below $60,000. Ether funds lost money every day of the week, and November's outflows now top $3.4 billion for bitcoin funds.

item.title: Bitcoin hits $55,780, lowest since September 2024, as crypto loses $216 billion in a day
item.description: Bitcoin dropped another 3.2% in one hour late Friday and ether fell to $1,559. Among CoinGecko's 30 largest assets, every asset fell except stablecoins and one tokenized loan product, and the whole market is back under $2 trillion.

item.title: Lighter's LIT fell 15% in a day to $2.31, its lowest price since August
item.description: LIT lost 5.8% in the same hour bitcoin broke below $60,000 on Friday and kept sliding into the evening. It is down 29% in a week, CoinGecko data show.

item.title: Bitcoin broke below $60,000 and hit its lowest in a year. Ether fell 5% in one hour, under $1,600
item.description: Bitcoin lost $2,277 in one hour on Friday morning and kept sliding to about $58,300 by 4 p.m. ET, a level CoinGecko's daily prices have not shown in 12 months. Ether briefly fell below $1,600 for the first time since early July.

item.title: Pearl fell 21% from its $2.35 high in 22 hours, then bounced to $1.98 as bitcoin slid
item.description: The AI mining coin hit $2.35 on Thursday morning, then dropped to about $1.85 by 8 a.m. ET Friday, with a 10.5% fall in a single hour. It is still up about 38% on the week.

item.title: Pi, Aptos, Optimism and four more top 250 tokens hit record lows as bitcoin slid to $61,273
item.description: Seven tokens worth $2.57 billion together set all-time lows between Thursday evening and early Friday, CoinGecko data show. Six are down more than 97% from their peaks.

item.title: SEC says fake crypto platforms took $37 million from 1,500 Americans, with SEC filings as bait
item.description: The SEC sued eight Colorado-registered entities on Thursday. Its complaint says WhatsApp groups steered victims into fake trading apps, then demanded fees to withdraw, while the money moved on to Tron.

item.title: Rumor vs record: bitcoin at $61,768 is still above MARA's $39,674 energy cost per coin
item.description: As bitcoin slid under $62,000, posts claimed it now costs more to mine a coin than it sells for and that miners are dumping. We checked five claims against price data and a large U.S. listed miner's own filings.

item.title: Thursday's ETF outflow revised sevenfold: bitcoin funds lost $632 million, ether $129 million
item.description: The first readings showed $90.8 million leaving U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs and $5.2 million leaving ether funds on Thursday. Revised data now put it at $631.9 million and $129.4 million, the worst bitcoin fund day of November.

item.title: Binance's wallets hold 680,028 bitcoin, 1.7 times OKX, Bitfinex, Bybit and Bitget combined
item.description: CoinMarketCap's reserve tracker counts $124.65 billion in Binance's listed wallets, including $30.2 billion in USDT and USDC. DeepSea's flow data show $1.55 billion more left Binance than arrived over seven days.

item.title: Bitcoin fell 3%, yet its Hyperliquid bets held at $1.23 billion. HYPE's shrank $64 million
item.description: Open bets on Hyperliquid's 179 crypto markets slipped to $3.25 billion, CoinGecko data show. Bitcoin's market did not shrink in five days, while HYPE and ether bets fell and Hyperliquid dropped from third to sixth by open interest.

item.title: Sky's USDS shrank $1.67 billion in one hour Thursday, and staked sUSDS lost 46% in a day
item.description: USDS fell from $8.45 billion to $6.37 billion in about a day, most of it between 11 a.m. and noon ET Thursday. Its savings version, sUSDS, dropped by $1.37 billion in the same stretch, while the dollar peg held.

item.title: Anthropic tokens hit $116 on day one, then fell 22%. Hyperliquid ANT bets traded $1.71 billion
item.description: On-chain versions of Anthropic shares peaked near $116 on Thursday and traded near $90 by Friday morning. Fewer than $4 million of the tokens exist, while bets on Hyperliquid's ANT market traded $1.71 billion in a day.

item.title: Zcash fell 14% and 30 top traders are 95% short. Influencer mk4 is short again
item.description: DeepSea counts $76.82 million of Zcash shorts on Hyperliquid against one $4.11 million long. Influencer mk4, whose $13.4 million Zcash short was gone on November 16, now holds a $4.60 million short.

item.title: NEAR fell 13% and top traders are 67% short, but the biggest bet is a $6.5 million long
item.description: Fifteen tracked Hyperliquid wallets hold $18.61 million of NEAR shorts and $9.32 million of longs. One trader, SM2902, owns most of the long side, entered at $2.14 and up $1.88 million on paper.

item.title: Solana fell 4% to $71.79, and 27 top Hyperliquid traders are 99% short with $89 million
item.description: DeepSea counts $89.41 million of SOL shorts against $1.33 million of longs. Two of the bigger shorts were opened at about today's price.
